title: Regular rank strata and their local face models
statement:
Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log regular scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. For $r\geq0$ put $X(r)=\{x:\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}\overline M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}=r\}$, using any geometric point $\bar x$ over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. The rank is independent of that choice. Each $X(r)$ is a locally closed regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] subscheme with its reduced structure. For $x\in X(r)$, let $A=\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $I_x\subset A$ be generated by the images of the nonunits of $M_{\bar x}$. The strict local ring of $X(r)$ at $\bar x$ is $A/I_x$. In a Zariski log chart the ordinary local ring is similarly $\mathcal O_{X,x}/I_x^{\rm Zar}$, where $I_x^{\rm Zar}$ is generated by its nonunit log sections. The connected components of $X(r)$ are regular integral schemes. A point $x$ is the generic point of its component precisely when $A/I_x$ is a field. Rank strata, their reduced structures, and this generic-point criterion commute with strict etale restriction. If $X$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian), only finitely many $r$ occur and each $X(r)$ has finitely many connected components.

Suppose in addition that the log structure is Zariski. For every $x\in X$ there is a Zariski open neighbourhood $U$ and a sharp fs chart $P\to M(U)$ inducing $P\simeq\overline M_x$, with the following properties. For every face $E\subset P$ (a submonoid such that $a+b\in E$ implies $a,b\in E$), the locus where exactly the monomials in $E$ are units is one nonempty connected rank stratum of $U$. Write $\eta_E$ for its generic point. These are all the connected rank strata of $U$. The map $\eta_E\mapsto P\setminus E$ is a homeomorphism from the set of these generic points, with topology induced from $U$, to $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. The characteristic stalk at $\eta_E$ is $P_E/E^{\rm gp}$, where $P_E=P-E$, and its generization maps are the corresponding face-localization maps.

source.place: VI 1.2 and 1.5, printed pp.69--70 (regular rank strata and strict-local equations); VIII 3.4.11, printed p.112 (local face models for the canonical stratum space). Supporting local geometry for ancestor lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve proof Step 3 through VIII 3.4.13.

proof.text: Work on a pointed etale sharp-chart neighbourhood $W\to X$ furnished by [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart]. For any ordinary point $w\in W$, let $F_w$ be the face of chart elements whose functions are units at $w$. The fixed-chart stalk formula [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] identifies the characteristic at EVERY geometric point over $w$ with $P_{F_w}/F_w^{\rm gp}$. Given any two geometric points over $x$, lift each to the SAME chosen $w$ over $x$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], applied to the jointly surjective family $\{W\to X,\ \mathrm{id}_X\}$ with $i$ the index of $W$ and $s=w$; restriction identifies their log stalks with the lifted stalks by [lem-trf-finite-monoid-stalk-data-spreading]. Thus their characteristic ranks agree. On any chart $Q$ write $\rho(F)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}(Q^{\rm gp}/F^{\rm gp})$; the characteristic rank is $\rho(F_w)$ by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening].

Fix finite generators of $Q$. Every face is generated by its subset of these generators [lem-trf-monoid-prime-minimal-neighborhood], so there are finitely many faces. If $E\subsetneq F$, choose $f\in F\setminus E$. Its image in $Q^{\rm gp}/E^{\rm gp}$ is nonzero: an equality $f=e_1-e_2$ would imply $f+e_2=e_1\in E$, contrary to the face property. This quotient group is finite free by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]. Hence its subgroup $F^{\rm gp}/E^{\rm gp}$ has positive rational rank, and tensoring the quotient sequence with $\mathbf Q$ gives $\rho(E)>\rho(F)$. Put $J_F=(\alpha(q):q\notin F)$ and let $b_F$ be the sum of the generators in $F$. The face property shows that $J_F$ is generated by the generators outside $F$. The locus with unit face exactly $F$ is $V(J_F)\cap D(\alpha(b_F))$: the closed condition excludes units outside $F$, and the open condition makes every generator in $F$ a unit.

source.place: VI 1.5, p.70; VIII 3.1.1--3.1.4, p.98. Finite-face argument expanding the chart description.

proof.text: On this chart the locus of rank at least $r$ is the finite union $\bigcup_{\rho(F)\ge r}V(J_F)$. Indeed a point with unit face $G$ lies in $V(J_F)$ precisely when $G\subseteq F$; this implies $\rho(G)\ge\rho(F)$ by step 2, and conversely one may take $F=G$. Thus rank-at-least-$r$ is closed on every chart. The chart maps cover $X$ and are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. A subset whose inverse images in this open surjective cover are closed is closed: the images of the complementary open subsets give its complement. Consequently $X(r)=X(\ge r)\setminus X(\ge r+1)$ is locally closed. Give it the reduced induced structure in the open $X\setminus X(\ge r+1)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. An etale pullback of this structure is reduced by [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] and has the same support as the chart rank locus; uniqueness of the reduced induced structure identifies it with the chart construction. This also proves compatibility of the reduced structures under strict etale restriction.

source.place: VI 1.5, p.70; expansion of local closedness and the reduced stratum construction.

proof.text: Here is the local algebra needed both for the reduced equations and for the Zariski face loci. At a sharp-chart centre put $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $A=\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{W,\bar w}$ and $B=\widehat A$. Interpret the geometric strict local ring algebraically using [lem-sbc-geometric-strict-henselization-local-presentation]. The completed-chart theorem [lem-trf-log-regular-completed-chart] identifies $B$ with its equal- or mixed-characteristic monoid model, possibly after changing the sharp chart while keeping the characteristic identification. The two sharp chart germs differ by units, as [lem-trf-chart-face-split-coordinates] with unit face $\{0\}$ and identity section shows; therefore they generate the same ideals $J_E$ for each face $E\subseteq P$. By [lem-trf-complete-model-face-quotients], $J_EB$ is prime, $B/J_EB$ is a nonzero domain, and $\alpha(p)\in J_EB$ exactly when $p\notin E$. The maps $R\to A$ and $A\to B$ are faithfully flat by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] and [lem-sc-strict-henselization-completion-noetherian]. Contracting each ideal successively by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] proves that $J_ER$ and $J_EA$ are prime and that the same monomial-membership criterion holds in $R$ and $A$.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), p.70; elementary ideal contraction from the completed monoid models.

proof.text: At $x\in X(r)$ choose the sharp chart $P=\overline M_{\bar x}$. Since $P$ is sharp, step 2 implies that $\rho(F)<r$ for every nonzero face $F$. Thus the inverse image of $X(r)$ on this chart is set-theoretically $V(J_{\{0\}})$. Write $J=J_{\{0\}}$. By step 3 its reduced ideal is $\sqrt J$. By step 4, $JA\,(=I_x)$ is prime. Every element of $\sqrt J$ therefore maps into $JA$, so $(\sqrt J)A=JA=I_x$. The strict-henselization quotient theorem [lem-sbc-strict-henselization-surjective-quotient], applied to the local quotient by $\sqrt J$, identifies the strict local ring of the stratum with $A/I_x$. This is regular by the log-regularity condition [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The ordinary stratum local ring is Noetherian, and regularity descends from its strict henselization by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-regular]. Therefore $X(r)$ is regular, by the local-ring characterization [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For a Zariski chart sharp at $x$ (constructed in step 8, which does not use this step), the same argument on the open $U$ with $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ in step 4 gives $\sqrt{J\mathcal O_{X,x}}=J\mathcal O_{X,x}=I_x^{\rm Zar}$, proving the asserted ordinary local-ring formula.

source.place: VI 1.2 and 1.5, pp.69--70. The nonunit ideal is identified by the chart pushout in VI 1.1.

proof.text: The regular scheme $X(r)$ is normal by [rem-pc-regular-normal](1). It is locally Noetherian, without any quasi-compactness assumption. Apply [lem-a1-normal-etale-components-clopen] to its identity etale morphism. Its connected components are irreducible open-and-closed subsets; their open subscheme structures are reduced and regular, hence integral and regular. On an integral component a point is generic exactly when its ordinary local ring is a field: in an affine domain the local ring at a prime $\mathfrak p$ is a field exactly when $\mathfrak p=0$ (injectivity of localization shows that a nonzero element of $\mathfrak p$ cannot become zero). For the stratum local ring $S$, the strict henselization is $A/I_x$ by step 5; its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_S(A/I_x)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-chart-maximal-ideal]. Faithful flatness and ideal contraction [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] show that this ideal vanishes exactly when $\mathfrak m_S=0$. This proves the field criterion. Under strict etale restriction, the characteristic and structure-sheaf stalk identifications in [lem-trf-finite-monoid-stalk-data-spreading] preserve $I_x$, so the criterion and the rank loci are preserved, as are their structures by step 3.

source.place: VI 1.2 and 1.5, pp.69--70; field criterion and locally Noetherian component argument expanding these descriptions.

proof.text: Now assume $X$ is Noetherian. Its quasi-compactness selects finitely many images of the sharp etale charts covering $X$; these images are open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Each chart has finitely many faces by step 2 and hence finitely many possible ranks. Their finite union bounds the ranks occurring on $X$. Every $X(r)$ is locally closed; its open ambient subscheme is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], and its closed reduced subscheme is Noetherian (on affine charts its rings are quotients of Noetherian rings, and a closed subset of a quasi-compact space is quasi-compact). Its topology is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], so [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] gives finitely many irreducible components. By step 6 these are precisely its connected components. This proves both finiteness assertions, using global Noetherianity only in this step.

source.place: VI 1.5, p.70; finite-chart and Noetherian-topology consequences.

proof.text: Assume now that the log structure comes from $M_Z$ on the Zariski site. Put $L=(M_Z)_x$ and $P=L/\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\times}$. The unit-extension formula [lem-trf-zariski-log-stalk-unit-extension] identifies $P$ with $\overline M_{\bar x}$, proves $L$ integral, and identifies its units. The group $P^{\rm gp}$ is finite free by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], applied to any fs chart at $\bar x$. Hence [lem-trf-integral-monoid-free-sharpening-splitting] gives a section $P\to L$ and $L\simeq P\oplus\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\times}$. Choose representatives of finitely many generators in $M_Z(U)$. The finite presentation [lem-trf-fg-commutative-monoid-finite-presentation] allows one to shrink the Zariski neighbourhood so that the finitely many defining relations hold, producing $h:P\to M_Z(U)$. Its geometric germ gives the associated-log-stalk isomorphism by the unit-extension formula. By [lem-trf-fine-log-stalk-chart-spreading] that germ extends to an etale chart by $P$. Compare this chart with $h$ after an etale refinement: the finitely many generator equalities spread by [lem-trf-finite-monoid-stalk-data-spreading]. Its image is an open neighbourhood of $x$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. On this image $h$ is a chart, since the chart pushout condition is checked at geometric points and every such point lifts to this refinement by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. Replace $U$ by an affine Noetherian neighbourhood therein. We have the required Zariski chart, sharp at $x$.

source.place: VI 1.1, 1.6 and 3.7(a), pp.69--70,75; VIII 3.3.4(ii) and 3.4.11, pp.107,112. Explicit Zariski spreading of a split stalk chart.

proof.text: For each face $E\subseteq P$ set $Y_E=V(J_E)\subseteq U$, retaining its quotient scheme structure. At $x$ its local ring is a domain by step 4 and no monomial in $E$ lies in $J_E\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Shrink $U$ so that all the $Y_E$ are integral, as follows. There are finitely many faces. Each $Y_E$ is Noetherian, has Noetherian topology [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], and has finitely many irreducible components [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. Exactly one component contains $x$, since distinct minimal primes contained in the prime of $x$ remain distinct after localization, whereas the local ring is a domain. Remove the other components, which are closed and miss $x$. The nilradical of the remaining Noetherian quotient ring is a finitely generated ideal and its localization at $x$ is zero; for each of finitely many generators choose a denominator outside the prime of $x$ killing it, and invert their product. Now $Y_E$ is reduced and irreducible, hence integral. Choose an affine neighbourhood inside this shrink. Performing these finitely many shrinks gives one common $U$. Each $Y_E$ still contains $x$, since the chart is sharp at $x$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.11, p.112, expanded using the completed models of VI 1.6, p.70 and a finite Noetherian shrinking argument.

proof.text: Let $b_E$ be the sum of chart generators lying in $E$. By step 2 the face locus is $S_E=Y_E\cap D(\alpha(b_E))$. It is a nonempty open subset of the integral scheme $Y_E$: each factor $\alpha(e)$ is nonzero in $\mathcal O_{Y_E,x}$ by step 4, so is a nonzero function on $Y_E$; their product is nonzero and the generic point $\eta_E$ belongs to this open. Thus $S_E$ is integral and connected, and its closure in $U$ is $Y_E$. Its points have rank $\rho(E)$ by step 1. If a point of rank $\rho(E)$ lies in $Y_E$, its unit face $F$ satisfies $F\subseteq E$; step 2 forces $F=E$. Hence $S_E=Y_E\cap U(\rho(E))$ is closed in that rank locus. The finitely many such sets at a fixed rank are disjoint and cover the rank locus, so each is also open there. They are precisely its connected components, with the reduced structure already constructed in step 3. This proves all the connectedness, nonemptiness, and exhaustion assertions. The argument includes $E=\{0\}$ and $E=P$; empty products are $1$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.11, p.112, using the elementary finite-face and integral-open arguments of steps 1--4 and 9.

proof.text: The characteristic formula [lem-trf-monoid-chart-characteristic-fan] gives $\overline M_{\eta_E}=P_E/E^{\rm gp}$ and the face-localization generization maps. To verify the topology, $\eta_F\in\overline{\{\eta_E\}}$ means $\eta_F\in Y_E$, equivalently $F\subseteq E$: at $\eta_F$ a chart monomial is zero exactly when it is outside $F$, since the defining ideal of $Y_F$ is prime and $Y_F$ is its closure. The prime ideals $P\setminus E$ and $P\setminus F$ have the same specialization relation, namely $P\setminus E\subseteq P\setminus F$ exactly when $F\subseteq E$. Both spaces have finitely many points (step 2), so their topologies are determined by specialization: the minimal open neighbourhood of a point is the intersection of the finitely many opens containing it and consists of its generizations. The bijection $\eta_E\mapsto P\setminus E$ preserving this relation is therefore a homeomorphism, as asserted.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.5 and 3.4.11, pp.98--99,112. Verification of the induced topology and characteristic sheaf.

tool_uses.why: Sharp etale chart existence; no perverse-unit lemma supplies the general logarithmic chart input.
Fixed-chart characteristic stalks and face-localization maps; the connected local stratum assertion is proved here, not taken from this generic tool.
Lifting arbitrary geometric points to a fixed point of an etale chart, for rank independence and the Zariski chart verification.
Restriction of geometric stalks and finite germ equality spreading; a generic sheaf tool needed for the chosen chart.
Free finite-rank characteristic groups and face quotients, needed for the rank comparison and stalk splitting.
Finite-generator face description; used to write the finite chart loci explicitly.
Open chart images, for descent of local closedness, finite chart coverage and Zariski shrinking.
Existence and uniqueness of the reduced induced closed structure on the rank locus.
Reducedness of etale pullbacks, so uniqueness identifies the stratum structures.
Identifies geometric strict local rings with algebraic strict henselizations, allowing the generic ring theorems to apply.
The ILO completed local model; the proof retains its permitted chart change and the mixed-characteristic case.
Unit comparison of sharp chart germs with the same characteristic identification, preserving all face ideals.
Primality and monomial membership for face ideals in the completed local model, rather than the desired connected-stratum assertion.
Faithful flatness for contracting face ideals and the maximal ideal in the field criterion.
Faithful flatness of completion of the strict henselization of a Noetherian local ring.
Contracts completed face ideals and detects a zero maximal ideal.
Strict henselization commutes with the local closed quotient; this is not contained in the definition of a strict local ring.
Descent of regularity from the strict henselization of the stratum local ring.
Regular implies normal under local Noetherianity; its globally Noetherian component clause is not used for arbitrary X.
Clopen irreducible connected components for a locally Noetherian normal scheme, applied to the identity morphism.
Maximal ideal of a strict local ring is extended from the ordinary local maximal ideal.
Noetherianity of the open ambient of a locally closed stratum, used only for global finiteness.
Noetherian topology for the finiteness and finite shrinking arguments.
Finite components for the globally Noetherian strata and the finitely many face closures.
Integral Zariski stalk and its unit-extension comparison with the geometric stalk, needed to build a Zariski chart.
Section of the sharp stalk quotient with free group completion; no freeness of the units is assumed.
Finitely many relations allow the selected Zariski generator germs to extend to a homomorphism.
A germ satisfying the log pushout condition extends to an etale chart; combined with the Zariski sections to obtain the required Zariski chart.
